single_variable: When the SpringBoard main thread's sync-reply destination has no receiver task, record the destination port's kind and disposition. Trial length back to 300s, late checkpoint 150s. ADT, root, FD and network-identity addresses unchanged from 6412899f.
diagnostic_page: fresh; run ID absent before boot and matched after
decoder_caveat: The probe tested ip_active before ip_in_limbo/ip_in_transit. In this kernel io_state_active() is true for every state except IO_STATE_INACTIVE, so 'active-no-receiver' covers IO_STATE_IN_SPACE with no resolvable receiver task, IO_STATE_IN_LIMBO(_PD) and IO_STATE_IN_TRANSIT(_PD). The port is known to be live, plain (not a service port, reply port or kernel object), and without a receiver task.
protected_storage: Data, Data metadata, root and log captures compared before/after under the fixed runner; no Android, Data, boot, GPT or root write by the trial
interpretation: SpringBoard's main thread waits for a reply that must come from a live plain Mach port whose receive right is not held by any task that can be resolved. The likely cases are a receive right still carried inside an undelivered message (in transit) or a port in the middle of a kernel move (limbo), for example a service endpoint that was never checked in or was handed to a job that has not received it.
next: This scope is consumed. The next probe needs a new scope and must check limbo and in-transit before active, record the exact io_state value, the destination's queued message count, and for in-transit ports follow ip_destination to the holding port's receiver task.
